title: Juicy German Cabbage Pilaf
description: A flavorful, fermented, and juicy German dish made with savoy cabbage and long-fermentation-dough, perfect for brunch.
instructions: Mix the long-fermentation-dough ingredients and let it ferment for at least 24 hours.
Chop the savoy cabbage and set it aside.
In a pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the caraway seeds.
Add the chopped cabbage and cook until it's slightly softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the apple cider vinegar, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Mix the fermented dough with the water and yeast, and knead for 5 minutes.
Shape the dough into a ball and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1 cm (0.4 in) and place it on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Spread the cooked cabbage mixture over the dough, leaving a 1 cm (0.4 in) border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the dough over the cabbage mixture to create a crust.
Bake the pilaf in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.
Let the pilaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
Slice the pilaf into wedges and serve warm.
